groups.closeConfirmDescription: Closing permanently ends all member conversations and cleans up any ephemeral agents. No further follow-ups or continuations are possible. This cannot be undone.
groups.continueHint: Re-runs all phases as a new round; every agent keeps memory of prior rounds. Attachments can't be added to a continuation.
groups.followupHint: Ask one member a direct follow-up. The agent keeps full context from the discussion; the exchange is added to the transcript.
groups.followupPlaceholder: Ask this member a follow-up question…

groups.hitlNotConfigured: No approval gates configured — click Edit to require human approval.
groups.moderatorlessWarning: Restricted to a moderator this group does not have: {{phases}}. The first member by speaking order will stand in.
groups.roleCoverageWarning: No member carries the role "{{role}}" — every member will speak in {{phases}} instead.
groups.phaseBehaviourNone: No abstention or convergence configured — click Edit to let members pass, or to stop a repeating phase once they agree.
groups.phasesNoneToEdit: This group defines no phases. Choose a discussion style, or add phases to the config, before tuning per-phase behaviour.
groups.allowAbstentionHelp: A member may decline to add anything new this round instead of restating itself.
groups.convergenceHelp: A judge compares each repeat with the previous one and ends the phase once the members stop moving. Costs one call per repeat.
groups.convergenceNeedsRepeats: Only available on a phase that repeats — a single pass has nothing to compare against.
groups.convergenceVerdictNote: After each repeat the moderator reviews the result against the question; the phase ends once it passes. A reply that is not a clear pass keeps the phase going.
groups.attachmentTotalTooLarge: Attachments exceed the total size limit
groups.convergenceInert: Configured, but this phase runs once — the judge can never run. Clear it, or give the phase more than one repeat.
groups.questionTooLong: A question can be at most {{max}} characters
groups.advancedNotConfigured: No transcript window, retro memory, shared artifacts or facilitator configured — click Edit to turn them on.
groups.contextWindowHint: Keeps each turn's context bounded on long discussions by folding older entries into a rolling summary.
groups.contextWindowSummarize: Summarize what falls out of the window
groups.contextWindowTruncateNote: Older entries are replaced with a plain "N earlier entries omitted" marker instead.
groups.artifactConfigHint: Lets members co-author documents that survive the turn they were written in.
groups.facilitatorHint: An agent that checks in at each checkpoint and picks one move from the list you allow — never a free-form orchestrator.
groups.facilitatorAgentRequired: Pick the agent that will facilitate.

facilitatorCheckpoint.EACH_REPEAT: After each round within a phase

groups.facilitatorNoMove: Allow at least one move, or turn the facilitator off.
groups.facilitatorMidPhaseNeedsRepeat: Ending or extending a phase acts mid-phase, so it needs the per-round checkpoint.
groups.facilitatorEscalateRequired: Escalation pauses the discussion for someone — name who.
groups.assignmentModeBid: By bid (members bid, highest confidence wins)
groups.assignmentModeRoleHint: The planner or config assigns each task, or round-robin.
groups.assignmentModeBidHint: Falls back to role assignment when an auction cannot pay for itself — fewer than two bidders or two open tasks, or too little turn budget.
groups.contextWindowSummarizerMissing: Without a summarizer model, overflow silently falls back to the plain truncation marker.
groups.facilitatorMaxMovesCeiling: At most {{max}} — the facilitator is a bounded intervention, not an orchestrator.

overview.roundScopeTitle: This view covers round {{n}} only. Earlier rounds are in the transcript.

groups.debateVerdictNote: Answers with a scoring verdict (winner and scores), not prose: {{phases}}. The members hold two or more roles and arguments come first, so the moderator's own synthesis prompt is not used. Set an input template on the phase for prose.
groups.retroCustomHint: A retro phase writes lessons into the team's memory, carried into later discussions. These caps bound how many.
groups.retroDefaultHint: A retro phase still writes lessons, with the default caps ({{perRun}} per run, {{stored}} stored). To stop it, remove the RETRO phase.
groups.voteOptionsTooFew: An explicit ballot needs at least two options.

taskBoard.emptyDescription: The moderator will create a task plan once the discussion begins.

groupServiceJudge.noteConfigured: One direct model call per check, no moderator needed. Its cost counts toward the discussion. A failed or unreadable reply never ends the phase.
groupServiceJudge.noteFallback: Name a provider and a model, or the moderator agent judges instead.

groupTemplates.advisoryBoardDesc: Five business perspectives — marketing, engineering, finance, legal, strategy — weigh in on the same question, then the moderator sums up.
groupTemplates.peerReviewDesc: Reviewers assess whatever you bring — a draft, a plan, a proposal — critique each other's assessment, revise, and the moderator merges the result.
groupTemplates.riskAssessmentDesc: Everyone gives their read, one member argues the opposite to expose blind spots, the others defend, then the moderator sums up what held.
groupTemplates.forecastingDesc: Members answer anonymously over several rounds and see only anonymized results in between, so no one anchors on whoever spoke first.
groupTemplates.proConDesc: Two members argue for the proposal and two against, followed by rebuttals and the moderator's verdict.
groupTemplates.negotiationDesc: Two parties state their interests, table proposals and trade concessions round by round; the moderator arbitrates only if no deal is reached.
groupTemplates.taskForceDesc: The moderator splits the goal into tasks, members work them in parallel, and the moderator verifies and combines the results.

choice.staticBody: One fixed header, the same for everyone — X-Api-Key, or Authorization: Bearer …
choice.basicBody: HTTP Basic. {{productName}} does the encoding, so the password stays a separate vault entry you can rotate on its own.
choice.clientCredentialsBody: The agent signs in as itself. One access token shared by everyone, refreshed automatically.
choice.authorizationCodeBody: Each person connects their own account and the agent acts as them. Needs sign-in to be switched on, and a vault.

connectionRef.wrapped: A connection supplies the whole header value, scheme included. Use ${connection:name} on its own and put “Bearer ” in the connection's header value instead.
connectionRef.headerMismatch: This connection sends its credential as “{{expected}}”, so the header must be named that — otherwise the config shows one name and the request carries another.
connectionRef.refusedInRequest: ${connection:…} is refused in a path, query parameter or body — a credential in a URL lands in every proxy log, and one in a body is not read. Reference the connection from a header instead.
connectionRef.refusedInModel: Language models, embeddings and vector stores do not accept ${connection:…}: a connection resolves to a whole header, and these need a bare credential. Use ${vault:…} here.
